questions.text: 'The Forgettle' (an electric kettle which switches itself off automatically).
questions.question: Identify the type of deviation in this brand name.
questions.explanation: It is a nonce-formation/blend combining 'forget' and 'kettle'.

questions.text: Gerard Manley Hopkins: 'Pitched past pitch of grief, / More pangs will, schooled at forepangs, wilder wring.'
questions.question: What stylistic device is prominent here?
questions.explanation: Hopkins uses heavy alliteration (pitched past pitch) to foreground the emotion.

questions.text: A Martian Sends a Postcard Home: 'Caxtons are mechanical birds with many wings. Some ___ are treasured for their markings.'
questions.question: What cohesive device is used to link back to 'birds'?
questions.explanation: The implied 'ones' acts as a substitute for 'Caxtons/birds'.

questions.text: 'Afghanistan is the land of Pashtuns. It always has been, always will be...'
questions.question: What does the modality 'always' indicate in this context?
questions.explanation: The usuality modality 'always' stresses an inescapable truth from a biased viewpoint.

questions.text: Amir's description: 'the one who went to school.... the smart one' vs 'he couldn’t read a first-grade textbook'.
questions.question: What is the stylistic effect of this contrast?
options: Positive self-presentation vs negative presentation of the other
questions.correct: Positive self-presentation vs negative presentation of the other
questions.explanation: Amir highlights his own intellect while stressing Hassan's illiteracy.

questions.text: A narrative element that answer 'What happened first?' and reports the ordered events.
questions.question: This element is called:
questions.explanation: Complicating action is the core of the narrative sequence.

questions.text: The desire to be free from imposition or coercion by others.
questions.question: In politeness theory, this is known as:
questions.explanation: Negative face is the desire for autonomy and freedom from impedance.

questions.text: A speaker says something manifestly untrue to create irony.
questions.question: Which Gricean maxim are they flouting?
questions.explanation: The maxim of Quality requires being truthful; flouting it creates irony.

questions.text: In the sentence 'I don't believe we've met'.
questions.question: The phrase 'I don't believe' is an example of:
questions.explanation: It expresses probability rather than a literal belief.

questions.text: Textual patterning involving identity of structure and contrast of lexical items.
questions.question: This is the definition of:
questions.explanation: Parallelism requires identity of form but contrast in content.

questions.text: Hopkins: 'the achieve of... the mastery of'.
questions.question: Using 'achieve' as a noun is a:
questions.explanation: It changes the word's grammatical class without changing its form.

questions.text: Omission of medial sounds in a word, like 'o'er' instead of 'over'.
questions.question: This phonological deviation is called:
questions.explanation: Syncope is the loss of sounds from the middle of a word.

questions.text: Conjunctions like 'however', 'on the other hand', and 'on the contrary'.
questions.question: These belong to which category?
questions.explanation: Adversative conjunctions signpost contrast or counter-expectation.

questions.text: The familiar association between content words like 'rabbit' and 'hole'.
questions.question: This lexical cohesion type is:
questions.explanation: Collocation is the habitual co-occurrence of words.

questions.text: 'It is a truth universally acknowledged, that a single man... must be in want of a wife.'
questions.question: This is a/an:
questions.explanation: It asserts a timeless truth about a whole set of people.

questions.text: A story element that bridges back to the present and may provide a moral.
questions.question: This is Labov's:
questions.explanation: The coda relates the story back to the 'here and now'.

questions.text: 'While I was waiting for the bus, it started to rain.'
questions.question: Which type of internal evaluation is 'While I was waiting'?
questions.explanation: Correlatives report secondary activities happening during the main action.

questions.text: Teacher: 'What is the capital of France?' Pupil: 'Paris.' Teacher: 'That's right.'
questions.question: The Teacher's second remark is which move?
questions.explanation: Feedback is the third move in a typical classroom exchange.

questions.text: 'I don't suppose you could give us a lift, could you?'
questions.question: Which negative politeness strategy is used?
questions.explanation: Expressing doubt about compliance is being pessimistic.

questions.text: Deviation measured against the norms of the general language system.
questions.question: This is:
questions.explanation: External deviation uses the language system outside the text as its norm.
